title: Palatine Capital Partners Management
quote: Thanks Zamir, let us take a look here and we'll be in touch.
action: Four minutes from send to reply, and he pulled in Caplan and Beckman. Both Betesh and Sacks passed on Canyon Woods purely on California, so there is nothing else on file blocking this one.

title: Managing Director, Strategic Advisory & Capital Markets
quote: Who is the seller? What is the current debt balance?
action: Answered the same hour - RAH, buying right at the loan balance. Diligence questions rather than a brush-off. Breakfast already set for 22 Oct.

quote: It's a good looking property and great basis. We are slowing on our RE investing right now while we watch cap rates reset with the recent rate moves.
action: A current ZMR investor, and the fourth firm to praise the basis on the way to no. Nothing about this deal is the problem - they are standing down on real estate generally until rates settle. Keep warm.

quote: Unfortunately too small for us (would need $25mm+ check to look) but appreciate you sharing.
action: The first objection in the other direction - every other size complaint has been that a check was too big. Rules Singerman out of anything at this scale; worth remembering for a portfolio or a larger asset.

title: Associate Director, Acquisitions
quote: Thanks bud. Houston still a challenge for us so going to sit this one out.
action: Market, not deal. Zamir has already proposed a New York catch-up off the back of it.

quote: Not for us. We don't do Houston. Only Austin and Dallas in Texas.
action: A clean geographic rule. Worth recording so Houston deals skip him and DFW/Austin ones reach him first.

title: Managing Partner
quote: Thanks Zamir but this one's not for us.
action: Same six words as Canyon Woods, and again no reason. Two unexplained passes in six weeks - the relationship is worth a call rather than another email.

title: Managing Principal
quote: What's happening with all the people that don't have a pass next to them?
action: Still the warmest name. He has the full no-fly list, has put his analyst on the file, and is now auditing the silent column - he wants to know which names are genuinely dead before he spends his own relationships on them. Answer it straight from this page: of 73 sent, 25 have come back and the rest are silent, not declined. He also said he is hearing the same Houston feedback through his own channels, which is outside corroboration that the blocker is the market, not our underwriting.

title: CIO / Executive Manager
quote: We reviewed the opportunity with our team last week, and the feedback has been positive. Everyone likes the story, and we are continuing to work through the numbers in more detail… there is one item we are working through on our side. We have a long-standing local partner in Houston with whom we remain actively invested… This does not reflect any hesitation on the opportunity itself.
action: Hottest name in the book. Clarity promised early this week — chase Wednesday if nothing lands. Chip owns the thread.

title: Principal
quote: Sounds great. Don't love houston but let's discuss.
action: Lunch is on the books for 30 Oct, but hold it loosely - Rami's son Gabriel arrived six weeks early on 10 Oct and is in the NICU. Lead with the basis when you do speak; he has already pre-registered the Houston objection.

title: Partner
quote: We do not currently have appetite for JV acquisitions in Houston but agree that the basis is strong (albeit small units). We will have a quick look and get back to you.
action: Seven days quiet since the 'quick look'. One nudge with the debt matrix attached, then let it go.

title: Associate, Investment Management
quote: The asset quality is there, but this isn't a market or submarket we're long on right now. The demographic profile was the biggest hurdle… median household income within 5 miles is ~$54K… leaves little room to grow rents over the hold. Rates were the other piece. With the 5-year Treasury up since the 9/21 lender quote, the deal starts with negative leverage at $34M. We're more constructive on Texas markets like DFW (northern corridor) and Austin.
action: The most useful pass we got. Two fixable objections: the $54K CoStar 5-mile median vs. the $71.2K on-site median, and negative leverage at the 9/21 quote. Rebut both in the next version of the memo.

title: Principal
quote: Looks like a good deal, but not a fit for us. Ronnie and I, and much of our investor network, were destroyed in Houston this cyle. Would take something very special to get us back in down there. Not totally opposed, but a going in 6%, even w upside, is not the answer for us.
action: Priced out, not disqualified. Would need a 6.5%+ going-in to reopen. Keep for a deeper-basis Houston deal.

title: Managing Director
quote: Tapped out on Houston right now (too much exposure).
action: Portfolio constraint, not a view on the deal. Same answer would have come from Kirsh's send. Re-approach with a non-Houston deal.

title: Principal
quote: Unfortunately, this one is not a fit for us as our fund exposure in Houston is maxed out at this time.
action: Fund-level cap. Revisit after their next vintage closes — nothing about this deal moves them.

title: Managing Partner
quote: It was a pass — Houston's a non-starter right now.
action: Flat market veto, no deal-level read. Nothing to rebut.

title: Investments
quote: We had a chance to review the opportunity… it is not a submarket we are currently pursuing or investing in.
action: Submarket-level no after a real review. Southeast Houston is the blocker, not the basis.

title: Principal
quote: Thanks for thinking of us, Andrew — we're not as focused on Houston right now unless it's affordable at Max rents.
action: Mandate mismatch — they want LIHTC/affordable in Houston. Market-rate will never clear here.

title: Principal
quote: Pass.
action: One word, no reason given. Nothing to work with.

title: Managing Director
quote: That is an unbelievable basis for that quality of product. Unfortunately, Midloch is out on Houston unless it is perfectly located in one of the pockets with phenomenal schools and uniquely high demographics.
action: The fifth firm to praise the basis on the way to no, and the clearest statement yet of the pattern: the asset passes, Houston does not. Their rule is a submarket screen, not a city ban - they would look at a Houston deal inside a top-schools pocket. Nothing to rebut here; file the rule and send them the next one that fits it.

title: Partner
quote: We'd like to have a good handle on how these properties have been renovated and where cash has gone before we evaluate additional acquisitions together.
action: Not an answer on this deal - an existing LP gating new allocation on reporting. Back from maternity leave and restarting a reconciliation she could not close before: NinetyNine44's $4.7M renovation reserve drew down to $638K by YE2021, then showed $1.2M at YE2022, and she wants that increase explained. She is asking, per deal, for a year-by-year reserve roll-forward, what each draw funded, and total capex by year and since acquisition. Zamir looped in Megan, who acknowledged at 16:41 on 13 Oct - 'we will get working on this and get back to you.' Acknowledged is not delivered; the reconciliation itself is still outstanding. This is the highest-leverage item on the board: it is the only reply where the blocker is ZMR's own books rather than Houston, and it is fixable.

title: Vice President
quote: Thanks for reaching out. Looping in Erin Sullivan who covers TX for us.
action: Filed as referred, but read it as forward motion: on Canyon Woods Rich's answer was that the equity fund was fully specified, and this time he routed the deal to Pearlmark's Texas coverage within three hours rather than repeating it. Pearlmark having a dedicated TX person is itself the signal. The next move is Erin Sullivan (esullivan@pearlmark.com) directly, not another email to Rich.

quote: Good to hear from you, Zamir. What is the seller's motivation here? Also, can you send over rent/sale comps?
action: Answered the same day. Zamir gave the seller motivation at 14:42 - the loan is maturing and the existing equity partner will not put in more to stay in and refinance - and Kevin sent rent and sale comps at 15:34, leading on how little competes nearby. Note that maturing-loan story is sharper than the broken process the teaser leads with, and both are true; consider which one the materials should lead on. Ball is with Niv now.

quote: We are going to pass on this one. We are pretty bearish on Houston based on our current portfolio and not focused on new deals there.
action: Both halves of the Houston objection in one sentence - existing portfolio exposure and a bearish house view. Their third pass in a row (Sarasota in January, Logan Farms BTR in March), and the first where the reason is the market rather than policy. Stop sending Houston; the relationship is still worth a non-Houston deal. Note the CC earned this: Scott Pearson is out of the country until 20 Oct and Chad answered in his place.

title: Chief Growth Officer
quote: I will run into a great deal of pushback on a fully occupied property at a 6% cap that nets to $135k a door in a $235k market. If we are going in fully occupied at a 6% on mostly new renters, all of the benefit needs to come from raising rents, so my argument needs to be that the prior owner was 1/3 below market. By the numbers themselves, it looks like a nice deal. Let me know your thoughts.
action: The sharpest read we have had, and it ends with a question rather than a no. Two challenges, both answerable only with evidence. First, he doubts the $235K comp from the outside: 3-4 bedroom homes near the site list at $150-225K, so the area 'looks relatively depressed' to him. Second, and this is the real one: buying fully occupied at a 6 cap means the entire return rides on rent growth, which only works if in-place rents are roughly a third below market - so prove the loss-to-lease. That is the fourth independent reader to land on rent growth and affordability after Sabal, Green Pine and Slocumb. Answer with the signed-lease trade-out record and an explicit loss-to-lease number, not with the IRR.

title: Director, Investments
quote: Thanks for sending. Do you have some time tomorrow afternoon to hop on a call to discuss further?
action: Booked. Brian sent a Teams invite at 21:00 for Wednesday 14 Oct, titled 'Call: Smart Living Allen Genoa', with Chip, Kevin and Michael copied. The calendar entry carries a -07:00 offset against an America/Chicago label, so confirm the hour against Brian's own CT wording before the day. He is the only reader in Houston, so expect the hardest test of the rent case: go in with Kevin's concession report (3.7% T12 to 2.6% T3 to 2.4% Y1), a loss-to-lease number, and a position on the 6.00% exit that Slocumb, Blue Vista and HIG all put higher.

title: Senior Analyst
quote: Regarding the addition of bulk cable / wifi, is there a contract for that? Do other assets in the market also charge for this income?
action: Kevin answered at 20:51 with market comps, and straight on the bulk wifi: quotes are still being gathered. That is the honest answer and also the exposure - there is no contract yet, so the one piece of upside in the plan that is not already in place is the one piece we cannot evidence. Worth getting a signed term sheet or at least a firm quote before Wednesday, because a Houston operator will ask the same question and the analyst has already put it in writing.

title: Senior Vice President
quote: While the per unit basis looks attractive, the T1 yield on total cost of 5.2% is below our comfort level. There is substantial growth in the year 1 NOI which we would hesitate to underwrite. The five year cash flow does not reach an 8% YOC even with the growth.
action: The most precise pass of the round, and the only one that puts numbers against ours. Two to answer before the Flagship call: she computes a 5.2% T1 yield on total cost where the teaser leads with a ~6% going-in cap, and she says the five-year cash flow never reaches an 8% YoC against our 7.0% untrended. Reconcile the first - cap on purchase price versus yield on all-in cost are different denominators and we should say which we mean - and decide whether 8% is simply a higher bar than this deal clears. She is the fifth reader to land on year-one NOI growth.

quote: This check is too small for us, and we're taking a pause on new investments for the time being. Digesting some recent deals and focused on asset management.
action: Size and timing, not Houston - he never mentions the market. Nothing to rebut; requalify when they are deploying again and only on a materially larger check.

quote: Unfortunately no movement on the JV front and Houston is tough for us in general right now. Let's catch up in the next few weeks to compare notes.
action: The JV position Zamir asked about has not changed, and Houston is a second strike on top of it. But he asked to compare notes in the next few weeks, which is worth taking - Forum sees enough flow to be a useful read on where equity is actually clearing.

quote: Unfortunately we aren't able to do non restricted market rate in TX right now. Most of what we do requires to have some sort of regulatory agreement or subsidy.
action: The affordability framing was the right instinct and still did not clear the mandate: they need an actual regulatory agreement or subsidy, not rents that happen to sit at 25% of median income. A clean structural rule - do not send them unrestricted market rate again.

quote: Would a Co GP structure interest you?
action: Not an answer on the LP ask - a counter-proposal. He is asking to sit on the GP side rather than write the $11.65M, which means he likes the deal and wants different economics for it. Worth a direct answer either way, and it is the third structural conversation now open alongside the extra GP co-invest offered to Flagship and the partnership framing sent to Halstatt. Decide what co-GP would actually cost before replying.

title: Principal
quote: The basis you secured coming out of the broken process is a compelling story. Where we land, though, is that we'd need to underwrite to an exit cap rate north of 6.50%, and at that level returns fall below our threshold.
action: The cleanest pass on the board and the most useful. The vintage objection that killed Canyon Woods is gone - he says so - and the whole thing now turns on one assumption: he needs north of 6.50% exit against our 6.00%. Slocumb said 6.25% independently. Two unrelated readers landing above our exit is a tighter, more fixable signal than the rent-growth theme, because it is a single number. Worth running the deal at 6.50% and seeing what survives before the Flagship call.

quote: I sent this around and the team wasn't interested, as this is a pretty rough pocket in Houston and not one where we'd look to invest.
action: Houston-based and the bluntest submarket read we have: 'a pretty rough pocket'. His Canyon Woods objection was no CA and no pre-2010, both of which this deal answered, and he still passed - so the vintage and geography fixes worked and the location inside Houston is what stopped it. Pair this with ARCTRUST on the $150-225K home listings nearby: two readers now say the immediate area, not the city, is the problem.

quote: If we are capturing most of the upside, our IC would anticipate the next buyer would warrant a higher going-in yield and thus cap rate expansion on the exit. Happy to discuss further on a quick call if you have time tomorrow. I'm generally free after 3p ET.
action: The second call of the round, and the sharpest version of the exit-cap problem. His logic is structural rather than a market view: if we harvest the loss-to-lease, the next buyer inherits a stabilized asset with no upside left and prices it at a higher going-in yield, so a flat 6.00% exit is internally inconsistent with our own business plan. That is the argument to have an answer for, because it does not go away if Houston sentiment improves. Note the clash - he is free after 3p ET, which is 2p CT, the slot Flagship first offered.

quote: We'd prefer to invest in a stronger market and submarket as the market stats don't look great, so it's hard for us to underwrite the MtM/burnoff plan.
action: The clearest statement of how the two objections connect: weak submarket stats are why he cannot underwrite the mark-to-market and concession burn-off, which is the entire business plan. Everyone else has raised the market and the rent growth as separate points; he says the first disqualifies the second. That is the argument to pre-empt on Wednesday, and the answer is the same evidence - signed-lease trade-outs and Kevin's burn-off report showing 3.7% T12 to 2.6% T3 to 2.4% Y1 as realised rather than projected.
